claims.statement: Five writable sync owners—Vault, Settings, Metrics, Connection History and Device—have separate engines, subscriptions and lifecycle state; History and Device share the deployed zone and record implementation but have kind-filtered journals and distinct consumer scopes.

Vault and Device follow the master iCloud switch; History, Metrics and Settings require their optional selections as well. Unset History defaults on and does not inherit the retired Vault preference or environment.
Desktop starts or pauses five sync owners according to Pro capability; mobile additionally requires an active scene and pauses all five on backgrounding.

CloudSyncLifecycle checks account binding and scoped safety/replica state, commits recovery before engine construction, reconciles eligible journal work and requires all current fetches to succeed before sending; local edits remain journaled while paused or fetching.

Lifecycle retirement invalidates its operation generation, cancels task and engine, clears send readiness and authorization and rejects old callbacks; fatal delegate persistence failure rolls back and retires the engine so a late completion cannot reopen uploads.

Account mismatch requires confirmation before engine creation; confirmation prepares old-scoped legacy quarantine and resets the owner's journal before binding the new user, dropping old tombstones/system fields and requeuing live records. Environment and ordinary-zone resets requeue category data without transferring scoped restrictions; destructive purge notifications instead retire and purge scoped cache.

Category journals retain versioned envelopes, tombstones, pending intent and CloudKit system fields; deterministic merges requeue local winners, scoped eligibility excludes blocked IDs without clearing intent, and save acknowledgement clears only the matching sent version if unblocked.

Fetched records and serverRecordChanged replies undergo the same validation and quarantine; supported reconciliation saves projection, journal/cloud metadata and unblock together. Physical deletion reconciles against durable replica state and may recreate a surviving local record with cleared system fields, still subject to upload restrictions.
Vault excludes device-local group/package expansion from wire projections, V33 Identity has no lastUsedAt, and Settings leaves debug/review and terminal typography preferences device-local.

Settings syncs credential references rather than secret bytes, marks accepted remote references iCloud-backed and migrates local secrets only with authorization from the current successful fetch under master and Settings selection; fetching, failure and retirement revoke authorization.

AISecretStore verifies an iCloud write before recording the iCloud location and removing the local copy, persists pending deletion before Keychain deletion, and retains the deletion marker to prevent delayed Keychain delivery from reviving a removed secret.
Settings uses distinct SSH, SFTP and workspace preference record types inside its existing zone so older clients filtering record types can ignore these preferences before decoding.

Safety storage scopes restrictions/recovery by container, environment, account, zone, owner and optional consumer; a new or interrupted scope forces a fresh cursor while retaining journal edits, with recovery committed before automatic engine/network work and held until safe completion.

Outgoing protection filters journal mutations, reconciles restored queue entries and materializes eligible saves/deletes synchronously after current-engine and restriction checks; storage errors fail closed, status separates partial restrictions and upgrade hints from corruption, and at most 250 combined materialized changes enter a batch.

Changed decoder capability forces scoped refetch for Vault and separately for History/Device consumers and checkpoints only after successful fetch/merge; Settings and Metrics currently do not pass capability IDs. This cannot retrofit unsafe historical binaries or make silently ignored V1 additions safe without a breaking version.

Native ConnectionHistoryItem and DeviceItem are written to the shared TermindConnectionHistoryV1 zone by separate kind-scoped owners; events can persist before Hosts, retain the newest 250 with terminal deletion/overflow tombstones, and clearing events leaves devices. Old Vault copies are cleanup-only, not continuously imported.

Both platforms present shared CloudSyncSettingsContent with headerless master toggle and aggregate status/actions followed by Optional Sync in History/Metrics/Settings order, without a separate Vault or Device switch; master enabling is Pro-gated and attempts Host password migration.

V28's local Host model stores SSH connection properties as `port`, `identityID` and `charset`; the V28→V30 lightweight migration retains those property names as SSH fields and supplies default-disabled Telnet settings, while the live Host projection supports separate SSH and Telnet profiles.
Local Host schema migration is independent of cloud format; VaultWireV1 freezes legacy Host SSH keys/defaults behind domain adapters and shipped Vault, History and Device writers remain V1.

The V28 compatibility fixture locally migrates and reopens a store twice through TermindPersistence.makeContainer, verifying SSH settings, default-disabled Telnet, associated Vault/History state and default workspace preferences; it does not test CloudKit replicas.

SyncRecordFormats declares per-kind read/write versions, with frozen Vault V1 DTOs and native History V1 fields; test-only Host V2 proves independent evolution. Record identity prefixes do not follow format upgrades, and encoding failures throw.

Structured cloud.sync.failed logging includes zone, stage and NSError domain/code without sensitive record/account content or localized descriptions; expected cancellation does not turn a paused or active owner into failure, and the legacy importer is retired.

CloudSyncRecordStateStore durably tracks presence, confirmed deletions and exact in-flight deletion incarnation so a crash or ambiguous delete cannot wrongly acknowledge a newer explicit device recreation; full inventory reconciles missing records before sends.

CloudKit purged and encrypted-data-reset zone notifications retire an owner's engine and purge scoped local cloud cache/metadata rather than recreate the zone; ordinary zone deletion instead resets and requeues the journal.

The Vault owner physically cleans obsolete History/Device VaultItem copies without importing their payloads or applying old-zone deletion increments to local events/devices; native History bootstrap does not reuse old Vault journal clocks or system fields.

Native HistoryCloudRecordV1 uses typed required metadata and event/device live fields, clears optional fields on writes and validates kind/format before interpreting native data; record identity does not change with wire format.
